subject: Finly discovery recap: p95 targets & streaming concurrency
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@finly.com>, Priya Shah <priya.shah@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Finly discovery recap: p95 targets & streaming concurrency

Thanks for taking the time today 

 great conversation. Quick recap from our discovery so we have alignment on pain, success criteria, and next steps. Please reply with any corrections.

Key pain points
- User-facing streaming UX is choppy for longer responses: token-level latency spikes when model emits many tokens (affects editor experience).
- Current infra exhibits high tail latency under load (p95s become unpredictable at peak concurrency).
- Cost and ops overhead of maintaining in-house optimizations (batching, VM sizing, fallback logic).

Current stack (what you shared)
- Inference: self-hosted endpoints running a fine-tuned open model on NVIDIA A100s (k8s autoscaling).
- Traffic profile: mostly text generation for summarization + chat assistant. Burstiness around batch job windows.
- Observability: Datadog traces, some token-level logs but sampling limits visibility.

Success criteria (what Finly needs)
- P95 generation latency: <= 200ms for short responses (<= 128 tokens) and consistent tail for streaming UX.
- Streaming UX: token start latency < 50ms and stable per-token latency for long outputs.
- Concurrency: sustain 400 concurrent sessions with graceful degradations and fallback variants.
- Cost target: reduce per-request GPU time by 20-30% vs current baseline.

Proposed next steps
1) You share a sample workload + traces (Datadog/JSON) and the current perf matrix (finly_current_stack.xlsx).
2) Redwood runs a sizing and a 2-week POC using Dedicated capacity to validate p95 and streaming behavior with your sample traffic.
3) Joint test plan: we'll run simultaneous concurrency sweeps, token-level latency traces, and failure/injection tests.
4) Pricing & timeline: if POC meets success criteria, we’ll scope Dedicated commitment and skip to procurement.

Attachments: finly_current_stack.xlsx (please confirm the sheet with traces).

Thanks 

looping Aditya/Ethan from our infra team for sizing and test-plan details.

Best,
Marissa Cole

Subject: Re: Finly discovery recap: p95 targets & streaming concurrency

Thanks Marissa 

 this looks right overall. Couple clarifications:
- P95 target: for our chat assistant we'd like <= 200ms for up to 64-token responses; for longer generation (100-300 tokens) we can tolerate p95 up to 400ms but streaming per-token jitter is the real blocker.
- Concurrency: the 400 concurrent sessions is our target for peak; sustained baseline is ~150.
- Cost: the 20-30% reduction is more of a stretch goal; reducing ops time (fewer incidents and simpler scaling) is equally important.

I'll upload the current perf sheet and a short trace export by end of day. Also looping Priya - she owns infra operations and procurement.









—Alex
